subject.title: [Feature]: publish host style variables to embedded MCP apps

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee the linked PR’s proposed subset and omission policy for host style variables as the public embedded-MCP-app contract?
rationale: The change is additive but establishes a public styling vocabulary, including intentional omissions for values the host cannot safely source; code review alone cannot choose the durable product contract.

options.title: Sponsor the proposed subset
options.body: Accept the additive subset and its explicit font omissions, contingent on real host-and-app proof and focused contract coverage.

options.title: Narrow the contract first
options.body: Limit the initial payload to a smaller semantic color and geometry subset, then expand only after a documented compatibility plan.

options.title: Defer to a token migration
options.body: Wait for Control UI to adopt the shared embed-token contract so the host can publish values without an interim mapping table.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the proposed subset
recommendation.body: Accept the additive subset and its explicit font omissions, contingent on real host-and-app proof and focused contract coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the proposal and its linked implementation rationale, making them the best available source for the intended variable-contract boundary.
